name: aux-boot-default
description: Half of boot to AUX; confirmed on hardware (NAV, 2026-09-28) together with aux-boot-restore (and aux-autoswitch). On its own it still boots to FM. C_MGR_SRC::StartUp restores the saved Last_Source into this+0xb4, the scheduler position ExecuteAllocationFirstRound matches each request's Sched_Pos against, with no validation. This edit replaces that load with a constant 7 (POS_AUX in C_MGR_SRC's scheduler-position enum), so the restore always targets AUX whatever the settings database holds. That survives source changes, unlike a Last_Source seed, which C_MGR_SRC::ImmediateSourceSave overwrites on every source change, and it needs no /USER_DATA payload. It sets the target only: AUX is selected when AUX's own boot request matches it, which is what aux-boot-restore enables. The Last_Source line in the C_MGR_SRC spy trace is written before this store, so it shows the saved value, not 7. NAV only: the StartUp address differs on the AUDIO_BT/AUDIO_BT_256 builds and must be re-derived. See docs/PATCHES.md#boot-to-aux-aux-boot-default-aux-boot-restore.
summary: forces `C_MGR_SRC::StartUp` to restore AUX (position 7) on every boot, ignoring the saved `Last_Source`

status.label: Confirmed with aux-boot-restore
status.note: boots to AUX with aux-boot-restore (2026-09-28, NAV); alone it still boots to FM

patches.why: C_MGR_SRC::StartUp boot restore: replace `lwz r9,8(r1)` (r9 = saved Last_Source, then stored to this+0xb4 / global 0x035e4cd0 / this+0xe4 at 0x01699490..9c) with `li r9,7`, so the restored scheduler position is always 7 (POS_AUX) instead of the value ImmediateSourceSave persisted. Makes boot-to-AUX sticky across source changes.
